title: AS2 compiler: switch uses abstract == instead of strict === for case matching
description:
In compiler.ts `compileSwitchStmt()` (line ~1062), each case comparison emits ActionEquals2 (0x49, abstract equality) instead of ActionStrictEquals (0x66, strict equality). Flash AS2 switch uses strict equality semantics — `switch (1) { case '1': ... }` must NOT match. The comment even says 'ActionEquals2 — strict equality' but 0x49 is NOT strict equality; 0x66 is.

The existing switch tests (switch.test.ts, switchstmt.test.ts, switchcase.test.ts) all pin on 0x49 being present, so they also codify the wrong behavior. The tests need to be updated to check for 0x66 (ActionStrictEquals) instead of 0x49.

Fix: change `this.emit(0x49)` to `this.emit(0x66)` at the case comparison site in compileSwitchStmt(), and update the test assertions accordingly.

Relevant opcodes (verified against ruffle/swf/src/avm1/opcode.rs):
  Equals2 = 0x49  (abstract ==)
  StrictEquals = 0x66 (strict ===)
